# Network analysis

This module turns relational data — an edge list or an adjacency matrix — into an `igraph` object, computes centrality and community structure, and produces publication figures with `ggraph`.

The helper lives in [`R/network-analysis.R`](https://github.com/connectors-testing-pplx/research-paper-template/blob/main/R/network-analysis.R).

## 1. Build the graph

```r
source("R/network-analysis.R")

net <- make_graph(
  edges      = edge_df,    # columns: from, to, [weight]
  directed   = FALSE,
  node_attrs = node_df    # optional: id, label, class, ...
)
```

For a co-occurrence network derived from survey responses, see `build_cooccurrence_network()` which computes a weighted graph from a set of binary items.

## 2. Summarize structure

```r
metrics <- network_metrics(net)
print(metrics)   # nodes, edges, density, components, transitivity, mean degree
```

## 3. Compute centrality and communities

```r
net <- add_centrality(net, measures = c("degree", "betweenness", "eigen"))
net <- detect_communities(net, algorithm = "louvain")
```

Centrality scores and community membership are attached as vertex attributes, so they are available for both plotting and downstream regression.

## 4. Visualize

```r
plot_network(net, by = "community", size_by = "degree")
# -> outputs/figures/network.png
```

## 5. Export node-level data

```r
node_table <- as_tibble_vertex(net)
write.csv(node_table, file.path(tables_dir, "network-node-metrics.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

## Where it plugs into the pipeline

`analysis/05-network.R` writes `network.png`, `network-node-metrics.csv`, and `network-communities.parquet` to `outputs/`. If your paper integrates LCA classes with the network, color nodes by `class` via the `node_attrs` argument.
